KANCITY — GENERATED DRAFT
(System Output)

FADE IN.

EXT. UNIVERSITY CAMPUS — DAY.

KAN, a freshman, arrives.
He feels joy.
He feels he belongs.
He meets his friends.
This initial joy is transient.

ACT I — A LIFE ALMOST REBUILT

INT. KAN'S HOSTEL ROOM — DAY.

Kan finds his wallet gone.
It held money and a number.
His friend calls him.
Strangers made contact.
They say they have his wallet.
His friend sends a number.
Kan is new on campus.
He has not left the hostel.
He does not know the roads outside.
He does not know these people.
The wallet holds money.
Classes end. He calls.
A voice instructs him. He must convene beyond campus boundaries.
He will get his wallet there.

ACT II — THE HUNT BEGINS

EXT. UNIVERSITY PERIMETER — 5 P.M.

Kan reaches the spot.
He observes a congregation. Numerous individuals are present. They exceed seven.
They stand.
They drink.
They wave him over.
They offer him a seat.
He sits.
They ask him to drink.
He says no.
The atmosphere shifts abruptly.
He knows he cannot refuse.
He drinks.
He tries to leave.
He declares his necessity to return to the residence.
This starts his deep involvement.
He is now tied to the Viking Brotherhood.
This group is the state's strongest cult.
It is one of the deadliest in the country.
He does not know one man is the killer.
This man is EMK.
Kan sees a pattern in others.
Rough men greet the group.
They greet EMK.
They use two hands.
This is a small gesture.
It means much.
It shows rank.
It demonstrates profound deference.
It shows fear.
Kan develops apprehension.
EMK acts differently.
EMK asks about Kan's studies.
It seems like a father.
It is kind.
Prior to Kan's departure, EMK provides his contact information.
EMK extends his numerical contact. He advises a call for any impending difficulty.

ACT III — WHAT HE OWES

EXT. UNIVERSITY CAMPUS — EVENING.

Kan leaves the group.
He feels relief.
He feels good.
He does not know.
He unknowingly agreed to something.
This will threaten his life.
It will jeopardize his academic aspirations.

FADE OUT.
